The pattern matches **mp-33444, Sr5(BiO4)3**, as the single phase present.

**What the pattern looks like.** The observed peaks fall at about 20.4°, 29.0°, a strongest group at 29.6–30.5°, then 41.5/42.0°, about 52–55°, and 60.5/61.7°. This is the pattern of a distorted perovskite-like cell with a large pseudo-cubic edge of about 4.3 Å. On that cell, (110) comes at about 29.4°, (200) at about 42.0°, (211) at about 52.1° and (220) at about 60.9°.

**Sr5(BiO4)3 (a = 6.03, b = 6.21, c = 8.58 Å).** Its calculated reflections line up with the observed peaks:
- (110) and (002) at about 20.5–20.7°.
- (111) at about 23.0°, matching the small peak near 23.3°.
- (020), (112) and (200) at about 28.7–29.6°, followed by (021) at about 30.6°. These match the 29.0° peak and the strongest group.

**Why the other candidates are rejected.**
- **ScMnO3 (mp-1105811):** it predicts strong peaks near 26.5°, 33.0° and 35.1°, and none appear.
- **LaY3Sc4O12 (mp-1222847):** its calculated peaks sit near 18.9°, 19.5°, 22.2° and 30.9–32.4°, which do not line up with the observed set.
- **Sr2TmRuO6 (mp-542767):** its pseudo-cubic edge is about 4.1 Å. That puts the low-angle pair near 21.6°, the strongest peak near 30.8° and (200) near 44°, all shifted from what is observed.
- **SrEuNbGaO6 (mp-1518126):** its pseudo-cubic edge is about 4.0 Å, giving the strongest peak near 31.6°, again too high.
- **Remaining candidates (Ti(FeO2)2, SmFe4(CuO4)3, Na4IrO4, Li2CoNiO4):** I did not calculate their peaks individually. A cell with an edge near 4.3 Å needs large cations such as Sr and Bi, so smaller-cation oxides like these would put their main peaks at higher angles.

**Uncertainty.** The (022) reflection of Sr5(BiO4)3 at about 35.7° is not seen, so it must be weak. I did not test whether the split peaks around 30° point to a second phase; I am treating them as the cell's own distortion.
